correctness.rationale: The full-part support lemma is valid: every color missing among fully colored parts must appear in at least two distinct partial parts, since each partial part has a zero vertex that cannot see its own colors. Thus w>=tm+2(k-c)>=tm+2 max(0,k-tm). For k=qm+s<= (r-1)m this yields the exact lower envelope qm+min(2s,m); the constructions attain it, with the q+1 full-part surjection possible since (q+1)m>=k and some blank part remains. Equality forces q complete distinct-color parts plus exactly two occurrences of each residual color when 2s<m, or q+1 complete parts with an onto palette when 2s>m; tie cases are disjoint. Named-color counts A=choose(r,q) k!/s! times the part-pair load sum of falling factorials, B=choose(r,q+1) sum_j (-1)^j choose(k,j)(k-j)^((q+1)m), and the s=0 count follow without automorphism quotient. High-palette case follows degree<k. Independently enumerated all named functions in 30 small (r,m,k) cases, reproducing both minima and number of minimizers. Small checks supplement the general support proof.

value.rationale: The balanced complete multipartite family is an elementary but natural regular graph model where every vertex outside a part shares a neighborhood, making palette redundancy and placement capacity structurally meaningful. The residue-dependent switch between duplicated residual colors and filling a further part, plus exact all-optimal-function enumeration, is a complete infinite-parameter classification useful for benchmarking algorithms and understanding singleton versus set-valued domination; it is not an arbitrary one-graph computation.
